text: Mutual information I(X;Y) equals zero exactly when:
explanation: I(X;Y) = H(X) − H(X∣Y) is non-negative and vanishes precisely when X and Y are independent — knowing one says nothing about the other. If X and Y were identical, I would be maximal (= H(X)); mere uniformity of X or determinism of Y does not by itself force I to zero.
